utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yugoslav.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But inside the former Yugoslavia your ethnic group, I mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Idbar in the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, what kind of schools did you attend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At four grades of elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked as an ordinary worker with four years of elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live at the beginning of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Idbar, where I was born.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who lived with you in your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mother, my old mother lived with me. We were the only ones in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Idbar a village with Croatian or Muslim or Serbian majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Serbs, Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I mean what was the majority? Was that a Muslim majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a Muslim majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately how many inhabitants did Idbar have at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only tell you the number of households. I don't know the number of inhabitants. There may have been about 130 Muslim households. As for us, the Serbs, 13 households, and there were less Croats, maybe four or five households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Can you say which is approximately the distance between Idbar and Konjic town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it's about 11 kms from Konjic to Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, was there a time when Idbar was affected somehow by armed conflict in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 9th March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say briefly what happened that day in Idbar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 9th May I was sitting with my mother, who was ill, my aunt, my sister-in-law, my brother and some more neighbours, who were having coffee at my place. Then we heard some shooting around the village. We did not know what was happening, so we got out into the yard, and we listened to the shooting that was getting closer and closer to our house -- to the houses, in fact. We stayed there. We waited until two unknown men in camouflage uniforms appeared. They had weapons in their hands. They told us that we should stay where we were and to wait. So we stood there. They approached us, and one of them stayed with us to guard us. The other one left. He went on from house to house. He was probably looking for people, for some particular people. That man who stayed with us to guard us told us that we should accompany him to the main road. We were in the village right next to the main road and there was -- this area was paved. When we -- when he brought us there we encountered three neighbours. They were already there waiting. These are Izedin Subasic, Mirso Nujic and Armin Nujic and the person who brought us was from Konjic, but I did not know his name. So they rounded us up there and I asked my neighbours, since I thought they would help me, to take me back home to my mother, since my mother stayed alone in the house and she was ill, or at least to allow me to take her with me, or to be allowed to go back home. My neighbours did not allow me. So I started to cry and I begged them, but they did not give me any answer, whereas this person from Konjic, whose name I do not know, he allowed me to go back to my home. I said that I did not dare to go back alone. I was afraid that somebody may think that I had escaped and I was afraid that I would be killed, so he escorted me all the way to my house, to where my mother was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I was there with my mother for a short while and then all the women came back and on that day nine men were taken away, the men from my village. Among them was my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say your brother's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Cedo Antic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know or did you get to know where was your brother brought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get to know that later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your brother was taken away with other men did you ever get to know where he was brought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is it why? Is that the question? Why he was taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where. No, we did not know where he was taken. After a month we learned that they were in Celebici, that they were detained in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know after one month that they were detained in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We asked. We did not know what had happened to them. So we asked where they were and what happened to him and a neighbour told us that they were detained in Celebici in the camp, in the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit your brother in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On one day when this neighbour of mine told me that they were in Celebici, I went there one day. I took him some clothes for him to change and when I came there I encountered a guard at the gate. I asked him for my brother. He did not give me any answer, so I asked him if I would learn anything about him and if I could hand over the clothes, since he had been detained for a month there without any change of clothes. He told me that he was not allowed to do so. He said that he should ask Delic if he was allowed to do that. So I waited there for a while and then he ordered me to go home, that he couldn't give me any assistance on that day. So I went back home on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, by the way, the name of this guard with whom you had talked on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know his name. His last name was Masic, so I did not know his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only time when you tried to visit your brother in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was the first time that I visited --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first time. Do you mean there was a second time when you tried to visit your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second time was on 15th June 1992, when an old woman from the village told me that they allowed for the clothes to be brought and that we could, therefore, go there and try to give them the change of clothes, and on that day, on 15th June, I went with three other old women to Celebici to try and hand over the clothes for them to change. When we arrived there, there were many other women who had come to visit their relatives. We waited there for a long time until we were able to hand over the clothes. When we were handing the clothes over, all this had to be searched and they had to check what we brought. If there was any food or some other articles, we were not allowed to do that. They only accepted the clothes. When we gave the clothes this was received by Muharem Masic and a guard stood next to him. This was a neighbour of mine, my next-door-neighbour. Izo Cosic was his name. Then the four of them gave them the clothes and we went back to our homes to Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, did you ask permission to see your brother on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I asked him. I asked my neighbour Cosic. I thought that he may be able to assist me to see my brother since I didn't even believe that he was alive at all. He told me that I couldn't, and he refused to talk to me any more. So I wasn't able to learn anything. When I came back my mother and my sister-in-law, that was my brother's wife, they asked me about him and I did not know what to tell them. I did not know if he was alive or not. I just said he have received the clothes. That was the only thing I knew and the only thing I was able to tell them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guard tell you why you were not able to visit your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He didn't give me any answer to that. He just said that we should go straight home, so that we left the area and went home. He didn't tell us anything as to the reason why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time when you were also arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the same day, when we came back home, the four of us, from Celebici, so I came home, I didn't know anything about my brother, whether he was alive or not. So we sat down and we discussed this and had coffee, and I went to my garden to do some work there. Then my mother went out with her cane into the garden. I helped her to get out and she then sat next to me. Then three men, three soldiers appeared. My garden was close to the house. They entered the yard, the three soldiers. One of them was a neighbour of mine, Zaim Cosic, nicknamed Paja, and two soldiers who were unknown to me. They told me that I should accompany them somewhere. Since I was in my garden and I was quite dirty -- I was wearing a tracksuit and it was all torn and dirty -- I asked my neighbour if I could go home inside the house to change, because I didn't want to go anywhere so dirty. He did not allow me to do that. He said that I wouldn't be detained for a long time, that I would be questioned and that I would then go back home. If I can just go back to -- this is something that I left out. When I talked to my mother and my sister-in-law about my brother, how I wasn't able to see him and how I didn't know anything about him, we again heard some shooting in the village. Again two uniformed men appeared at our gate. They wore camouflage uniforms and they had rifles. They were leading a neighbour of ours, Milorad Jovanovic, with them. They came to my gate, to my yard, and they asked for me. I left the house. I stood in the yard at the gate, and they told me that they should enter the property and search my house. They said that there was some kind of a radio station or a transmitter in my house. Since I didn't know anything about that, I was there and they told me to take them inside the house. I went inside with them. They drove me out of the house while Armin Nujic guarded me in front of the house in the yard and Milorad Jovanovic, and as for Dzevad Alibasic, he was searching my house. He was looking for the transmitter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That happened a little while before they came to arrest you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I had left that out. I forget that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So they searched the house. They didn't find anything. So Dzevad Alibasic left the house and they went on. Milorad Jovanovic went with them, so they got out of my yard. That's when I went to the garden to dig the potatoes. My mother was there with me. I had led her out into the garden to watch me while I worked, and that was when the three soldiers appeared, the soldiers I mentioned a little while ago, Zaim Cosic, nicknamed Paja, and two unknown soldiers. This was when Paja told me to accompany them. That's when I asked him if I could go inside the house and change, since I was very dirty. I didn't want to leave the house in that condition. My tracksuit was all torn and dirty. He did not allow me. He said that I -- that it wouldn't take long, that I would be back home soon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, can you say whether these persons who apprehended you had any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were all in camouflage uniforms and they all were armed. They carried weapons in their hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some insignia, but I did not observe that. I did not dare to look, so I wasn't able to discern the insignia. Since these were all my neighbours it was an unpleasant situation, and I didn't want to look. So I did not remember the insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told why you were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked my neighbour Zaim when they were taking me, and he said that there was a transmitter at my place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any weapon at the time of your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether your brother or anybody else in your family had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in any way take part in the defence of the Serbian houses in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximately say how many persons, if any, in your village were armed at the outbreak of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is not something that I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mrs Antic, where were you brought after you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went with the three soldiers, I encountered at the main road, they had rounded up three men and a woman. The fourth was Milorad, who had been with the people who had been to my house. So that there were four men and one woman and myself. I was the sixth person to be brought there. When I was brought there I encountered them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "there", Mrs Antic, where were you brought actually after your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought us to the main road where they rounded us up the first time, when they had taken us away. This is the main road. When I say the main road, that's the blacked up road leading through the village, through the entire village. That was the main street, the main road, and that's where they rounded us up. There was already a car waiting for us. So that's where they searched the men. If they had any documents, these documents were seized, and then they ordered us to get into the car that was already there waiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that where did they bring you with this car, if anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we got in that car, the car went to Celebici. As we started there was a small car behind us. It was driven also by a next-door-neighbour of mine, Sefik Omerovic. He escorted the car in which we were. He followed us and two unknown soldiers with us on the car, on the vehicle and Izo Cosic, the third person who was with them, he went back. So we were escorted by just these two soldiers to Celebici, to the camp, where we were brought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, can you say approximately at what time of the day did you arrive at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was somewhere in the afternoon. I do not know exactly when, more towards the late afternoon, early evening, but I do not know exactly the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are just talking about 9th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We are just talking about 9th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No, this is not any more 9th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was 15th June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You are welcome. Would you now say in some detail what happened as soon as you arrived at Celebici? I mean, on the very first day of your arrival there, in the afternoon of 15th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we drove into the Celebici camp, the car pulled up and some soldiers came. They were looking us who were in the car, and they did not let us get off. They were saying that a person named Delic had arrived. We did not know who he was. They were waiting for him to come. Then he came there, that person, and he took a pencil and a piece of paper and he started to write down our first and last names. When he made the list of our names he told us to get off the car. We got off. Then he separated men from us women. The men were taken in one direction and a soldier took us two women into another direction. He took us into a room where we found some other women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment, Mrs Antic. When you say about Delic, how did you get to know his name? I mean, how did you get to know the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We only heard from those soldiers who were there to watch us while we were in the car. They only watch and said: "We are waiting for Delic to arrive". That is how we learned about it but at that time we did not know who that man Delic was. We only heard the surname from them. We only later -- learned later on who Delic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you learn later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learned later on that Delic was the Commander of that camp that existed there in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mrs Antic. You were saying something. In which building of the Celebici camp were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Us two women, we were taken into a building. We called it the reception building. It was situated -- located near the gate, towards the entrance of the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were already other people inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When that guard brought us to that building we found four women there, four women from Bradina, and a fifth woman was Grozdana. Then the two of us arrived, so we stayed there with them and the guard went back. He went out of that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did anybody interrogate you on your arrival at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We sat down for a while, maybe for a short period of time. I do not know exactly for how long. A guard came to the door and he said to me and to this other woman, Ljubica, who was there with me, he said: "These two women who came only a while ago, could they please go out?" We went out then in front of the door. There stood four men wearing camouflage uniforms. Some of them had weapons and I am not sure whether all of them were armed. Then they started interrogating us. They asked us also for our first and our last names. They asked us where we were from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who were these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One person, the one person I knew best, was somebody who used to work in the same company as I did. He was a guard and his name is Sejo Mustafic. There was Delic, there was Mucic and there was Delalic there. First Pavo started to question me, Pavo Mucic. He asked me where I was from, who was my family. He asked me where my husband was, and upon that I answered that I was not married, that I had no husband. He said to Delic: "This is just the right type for you." Delalic asked me about Srecko Antic. We had the same surname and he asked me: "And where is Srecko?" Then they did not ask much more that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn the names of these people that you just mentioned? I mean, how did you get to know the names of these persons, particularly Mucic and Delalic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Delic or Delalic, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: She mentioned Delic, Mucic and Delalic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delalic, yes. As for Delalic, Sejo Mustafic told me about him several days later, that that had been Delalic, because I did not know him from before and I never saw him afterwards. That was the first and the last time I saw him in the camp. So Sejo Mustafic told me that that was Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mucic? How did you learn his name? How did you get to know that this man was Mucic, the one who specifically questioned you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about him when I was there later on. I heard about Mucic, that he was one of the heads of the camp, but I did not see him. I mean, the second time I saw him was only when he came to release the women from Zukici that spent one evening with us. That is how I learned that he was Pavo and that he was some kind of a chief there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get to know also the first name of Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in which capacity did they ask you those questions? I mean, which role did they have for interrogating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the other woman also interrogated in the same occasion and place? I mean, which questions she received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they ask her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked her also her name, her surname, whether she had a husband, whether she had any sons, but her son and her husband were also brought at the same time as we were to the camp. So she was asked which one was her husband and which one was her son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly who was the one who asked these questions to this lady?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mrs Antic, did anything happen after that and during the first night after your arrival in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They ordered us to go inside. We went inside and that night it was dark. We were not allowed to put the lights on. Somebody came to the door and opened the door and said -- he called me out. He said my name, first and last, and told me to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I did not know. When the person was still at the door and while I was still inside the room I did not know who he was. Yet when I asked him whether I could stay in and leave everything for tomorrow and then go out, he told me: "No" and said I had to go out straightaway because the Commander was looking for me in order to question me. When I came to the door, I had to go out. I recognised him. His name was Muharem Masic. I asked him where he was taking me and he told me that the Commander needed to question me. Then he took me into another building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took me into that building. There was a very large corridor with many doors. He brought me in front of a door and then he opened the door and took me into that room, where we found Delic, who was sitting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which building was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That building was not far away from the building in which we were placed. That was probably the building -- I mean, that was the building with their command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask her to indicate it on the plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask her to indicate this on this model.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I will reach that later, your Honour, if you allow me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you said you arrived to a given room inside this building, and can you go ahead with your account?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Then Masic returned and I stayed there. Delic started to interrogate me. He questioned me again about my first name, my last name, where I was from, why I was brought there. I did not know what to answer. He started to curse. He said that the Cetniks were guilty for everything that was going on. He started to curse my Cetnik mother. He told me that unless I did whatever he asked from me that he would send me to Grude, where a Croatian camp was, or else I will be shot. I started to cry. He ordered me to take my clothes off. I was constantly imploring and crying and asking him not to touch me, as I was a sick woman. To no avail. He started to threaten me with his rifle, saying that he would kill me. He pointed the rifle at me. I got scared. I was afraid he would kill me. So I had to do what he asked from me. I had to take my clothes off as he pointed the rifle on me, on the upper part of my body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, was the light on in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Delic wear a uniform in that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead in your account. What happened right after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me then why did I not dress more nicely, as I came all torn and dirty from my garden. He asked me why I wasn't dressed nicely. I did not know what to answer. I said: "I was not allowed to go into my house". Then he threatened me. He ordered me to go into the bed and to lie down. Then he raped me. He ordered me to take my tracksuit off. I had a jumper, which I also had to take off. Then I had to go on the bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry to ask you that, but could you please give us some more details about the rape. Did he -- can you give us some more details on the very event of the rape, if you don't mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I then had to climb in the bed. Then he took his belt off. On his belt he had a pistol. So he took some of his clothes off and climbed into the bed and then he started to rape me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, did he penetrate your vagina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ejaculate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he do that inside your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the lower part of my stomach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately how long did all this last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know for how long. It seemed very long to me. I don't know. When I was returned back to our room we did not have any watch. We were not allowed to put any lights on. I don't know how long it lasted but too long for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything else to you during the rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He only threatened me, cursed me and he threatened me, saying that I would be killed and so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened right after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that he got off -- got up and got off the bed. He put his trousers on, went out of the door and told me to get dressed. I got up and got dressed. Then Muharem Masic came in and he brought me back to the room where we women were staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say anything to the other women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not say anything about that. I was all in tears. They could not see because it was dark. I only said: "Oh, fuck you, God, in case you exist. Why did you not protect me from this?" I thought it would help me to feel a bit more at ease. That was the only thing I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did you have occasion to see Delic again the following day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The following day he came at the door. He opened the door and he only said from the door -- he asked me how I was and how I felt. I was looking right in front of me and started to cry straightaway. He said: "Why are you crying? This will not be your last time".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I felt so miserably, I was constantly crying. I was like crazy, as if I had gone crazy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said this happens, this visit happens at the door. Which door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came at the door of that room where we women were staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean at the reception building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken back to that room in the reception building. That room where other women were also, so I was returned to those other women into that room, into the reception building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, Madam, how long did you stay in this reception building at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed until 31st August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the four women from Bradina stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The four women from Bradina, which I found thereupon my arrival, when Ljubica and myself arrived, they only stayed there for one night and the following day they were released to go home. So only Ljubica, myself and Grozdana remained there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who came and picked them up, I mean the four women from Bradina from the reception building when they were released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A guard came to the door and he told them they could go home. So they prepared themselves, went out and I did not see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only saw a guard coming to pick them up and you do not know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know which guard was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I do not know, because they were constantly changing. They were always new guards, so I do not know who that guard was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did Ljubica Jovanovic stay at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were brought on 15th June. I think it was a Monday, and she was released on Friday, so she was with us for four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who came and picked her up from the reception building when she was released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also a guard, a guard who came and told her she could go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did you suffer other sexual assaults after the one you just described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One day it was daylight. Delic came at the door and with a very rough voice he ordered that we had to go into the command building, that we have to wash there, take a bath. We asked not to go there, to have a bath in that other building, that we could do it where we were in the reception building, and he said that we should go there into that building where the command was. Then he came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean only you or both of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both of us, yes. Myself and Grozdana, because there was nobody else there, just the two of us. He told us that both of us had to go to the building where the command was to have a bath there that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to have of a clear idea immediately, how long did this happen after the first rape approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't tell you exactly how many days had passed. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead in your account of this second sexual assault?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic then closed the door to our room and left and after a short while Muharem Masic came at the door of our room in which we were and he said that we had to go with him to the building where the bathroom was and that we had to have a bath. He said that he had been ordered by Delic to bring us there. We had to go with him. He took us there, to the building where the command was located. He brought us in front of the bathroom and he told Grozdana to get in, to be the first one to take the bath. Grozda got in. She had a bath and she got out. Then he ordered me to get inside. I got in. I started to have my bath and then Muharem got into the bathroom where I was having my bath. I started crying. I was begging him to leave while I was in the bath. He told me that he had to go in to tell me that I had to take a really good bath to wash myself very clearly, very much because some doctors would come to examine us. Then he left the bathroom. So I had my bath and I got dressed and when I left he was waiting for me at the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He? Who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muharem Masic. He was waiting for me at the door. When I left and encountered Masic, he led me down the same corridor towards that same room in which I had been once before, where I was raped for the first time. He took me there. He opened the door. I saw that it was the same room where I had been raped already. Delic was sitting there. He was sitting at the desk. He was sitting at the desk that was there and when I got in Masic returned. Delic then asked me if I had had a good wash. I immediately started crying. I was afraid that the same thing would happen as the first time: he then ordered me to take off my clothes. I kept saying that I was sick. I was telling him not to touch me. Since he again had a pistol and a rifle I was afraid that he would kill me, so I had to do it. I had to take off my clothes. So when I took off my clothes he told me to get on the bed. Under duress and his threats I got on the bed and then he told me in which way to turn, how to position myself. He told me to turn around and to kneel. He climbed on to the bed then and he started to rape me in my anus. I started to cry. Actually I did not cry. I screamed because it hurt very much. He did not rape me in the anus. He then turned me on to my back and then he raped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, again did he wear a uniform, Mr Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was always in a uniform and he was always armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the rape was he completely undressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He would just pull down his trousers. The first time he just took off his shirt and he was in his vest, undershirt, and the second time he just pulled down his trousers. He did not take off all his clothes completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he actually penetrate your anus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It hurt me very much so he wasn't able to penetrate me fully. I started to bleed. My anus started bleeding, so he let me go, turned me on to my back and then raped me into my vagina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he penetrate your vagina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ejaculate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, again on my lower abdomen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened right after this second rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the second rape again he called Muharem Masic to take me back to the room, to the reception room, where we were. Grozda was already there. When he took me there, when Muharem Masic took me there to our room I was all cried out. I did not tell Grozda anything. She saw that something had happened to me and I went to the toilet and I put cold compresses on the anus because I was already bleeding. I was very ill. I was crying all the time. So that next day Grozda had to seek a doctor to see me. She asked a guard to ask the Commander whether a guard could come to me because I was so ill. Then one of the guards came and brought two doctors with him. These doctors were also detainees. They were prisoners in the camp. These are Relja Mrkajic and Petko Grubac. So they brought them there. A guard brought them there. They came. They measured my blood pressure and they brought some tranquilisers, some pills. They asked what had happened to me. I couldn't tell them. I couldn't tell anyone about that. So that they gave me those medicines and they went back. In fact, the guard took them back from where he had brought them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right after the second rape did you realise your anus was bleeding during washing yourself? Did you have another shower after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I had to go to the toilet often and I realised that my anus was bleeding. I didn't tell Grozda about that. I just put some kind of cold compressions and I asked her to give me some kind of ointment, because she had a bag, a purse with her, and she had some cream in the bag. So I asked her if she had some cream and she gave me something so that I had to apply this cream without telling her what had happened to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell her anything at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not tell her anything about that. I just told her that this was the first time that I had been with a man. She then told me she assumed what had happened to me and she asked me if I needed pills, the pills that she had been taking. She had been taking them even before the war. These were, I guess the birth control pills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, one question about this second event, about the room in which this happened in the administration building, in the command building. Can you say which part of the camp could you see through the window of the room in which the second rape and actually also the first rape happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing we could see through that window in that room, I could only see the reception building where we were located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was this second rape the last sexual assault you suffered in Celebici? Was there any other sexual assault after these ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there was the third time. It happened in our room in the reception building, where we all were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom were you raped this third time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again by the same man who did it twice before, and that was Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mrs Antic, before going ahead in your account about the third rape and in order to maintain a rational order in your account I would like you first to answer some questions about the reception building in which you stayed during your detention in Celebici. Let us start from the room where you used to sleep. Did this room have any window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the window of this room where you used to sleep in the reception building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a large window and there were bars on the window. It was actually some kind of wire. I don't know how to describe it, what to call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of the camp could you see through this window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the room, is that what you mean? From our room?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, from the room looking out through this window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see the entrance gate and the road. That's what we could see from our window, the road leading down to the village of Celebici. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Excuse me. Can we have a break for at least twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Of course, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The Trial Chamber will rise and reassemble at 4.15. (3.45pm) (Short break) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please invite the witness. (Witness returned to court) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Kindly remind the witness she is still on her oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Madam, right before the break you were describing the room where you used to sleep inside the reception building. Can you describe the furniture in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an iron bed. There was also a wardrobe of some kind and there was a hanger where you could hang your coat. There was a mattress on the floor, where one could sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that in the very first night you were seven women in that room. How did you sleep there with only one bed and one mattress?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three of us slept on the bed and four slept on the floor, on that mattress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, how many doors were in this room where you used to sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two doors, one that was used and we entered and exited the room through that door and there was the other door and this wardrobe was against that door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the second door was actually not used; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I mean, yes, it was not used. Only one door was used and we got in and out through that door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these two doors located in the same wall or in two different walls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the same wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the door which was actually used? Was that usually kept open or closed or locked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was closed but not locked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which kind of a door was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door was made of wood, of planks. So it was not a glass door but a wooden door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this door lead to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door on our room where we were led to a large corridor that was in front of our room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any furniture in this other room which you call a large corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was some kind of a wooden desk or a table, and I think that there was also a chair, and you could sit down on that chair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this room normally used for, this what you call large corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, while we were there it was used by the guards who would stand guard. They would spend the night in that corridor while they were on guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many windows did this room have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which kind of windows were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were not large windows. They were medium sized windows, neither large nor small.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, were there glass windows? Did they have bars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No, there were no bars, but they were glass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of the camp could you see through these three windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through one of the windows we could see the entrance gate leading to the compound, to the camp compound. Through the -- through another window we could see a large wall and above that wall there was the village, the houses and the third window looked on to the Tunnel Number 9 in which detainees or prison inmates were also located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the second window looked to a wall, was that wall inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, was the main entrance of the building visible from any of these three windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the window in the corridor, in the room that we call the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the window that faced the gatehouse, or the window which faced the wall, or the window which faced Tunnel 9?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the window that looked on to the entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you would get into this -- I beg your pardon. Was there any other door in this second room, the so-called large corridor? I mean, any other door besides the one which led to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a door leading to a small corridor that was located in front of this large corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you would get into this third room, which you call a small corridor, how many doors would you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was one door leading to the toilet and a second door was leading out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the main entrance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, towards the yard and then further on to the entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the door which was not used and which should have led to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was also in the small corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now please describe the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you get into the toilet, there is a tap with water. We could wash there our faces and there was a washbasin underneath the tap. There was another door there leading to the toilet itself and there was a squatting toilet. There wasn't a toilet bowl. So that there were two doors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any window in the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a small window in the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of the camp could you see through the toilet window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we could not see anything because the window was very high up in the wall. It was high up so we couldn't see anything through that window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, was the main entrance of the building usually kept open or closed or locked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The door was half made of glass and half it was not made of glass. It was not locked, but it was closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could the guards prevent you from escaping then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the guards were always changing there and there was always somebody standing guard there over us. We were always under guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now if I should show you a map of the reception building, do you think you could recognise it and orientate yourself on such a map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I might be able to. I am not sure, but I will try to orientate myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I ask the usher to provide the witness with exhibit 1. I think it is page ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe 14. MS VAN DUSSCHOTEN: Page 4. THE USHER: On the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: On the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not very clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not very clear to you. Okay. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Show her the photographs. Maybe she can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour wants us to show her the photo, photograph number 5 and Number 6 I suppose of Exhibit Number 1. Do you recognise the building? Did you recognise anything in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the building you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can see, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, if you should see a model of the Celebici camp, would you be in a position to orientate yourself and recognise such a model? You see a model in front of you. Could you recognise something in that model? You can stand, Ms Antic, to see it better, if you wish?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is not the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. It does not matter. You can sit down, Mrs Antic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This was made about four years after the events. Maybe there has been some repainting, maybe some changes possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Maybe she needed -- anyway ... Madam, before going back to your account can you please tell the court whether you had any other occasion to see Mr Delic between the first rape and the second rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would often see him in the courtyard, in the compound. He would be walking around. He used to sometimes come to our door just like that. He would open the door and then sometimes he would say something to us. Sometimes he would just turn. I saw him when women were brought from Zukici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From when -- from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the village of Zukici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us details of this event, the coming of women from Zukici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One evening Grozda and myself were in that room where we to be, and we heard female voices and females moaning, and then we asked each other maybe somebody would come to us so we would not be alone any more. Then after a relatively short period of time -- I don't know how long afterwards -- four women were brought in at the door and they put them into our room. Those women were brought by some guards. Then the lights were put on, because we were never allowed to put the lights on. We were always in the dark. Then the guards who brought them put the lights on, so we could see that those women were heavily beaten. An elderly woman, the oldest one among them, was so severely beaten that she was not even able to see with her eyes. Then they put them with us and with the guards that brought them were accompanied by Delic. We were there then. This elderly woman, the one who was severely beaten, asked some help from us. She often she asked us to take her to the toilet. Grozda constantly kept taking her to the toilet. She asked us something to eat, saying that she was hungry. We did not have anything to give to her. After I don't know how much time a fifth girl was brought in. She was a minor. She might have had 12 -- she was 12 or 13 years old. They put them there, brought them to us. At that time they were threatening them, cursing. They cursed their Cetnik mother and then they left them with us and they spent the night with us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, can you say when did that happen, on which day, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That happened somewhere in July. I do not know on what day it was of the week, but I remember the date. It was 12th, because I knew one of the women. I recognised her when they put the lights on, because I knew her from before. She was a relative, an in-law of my sister's, and as I knew her I asked her why they were brought here. Then in a very low voice, because we were not allowed to talk, so she whispered into my ear and told me that they were arrested because on that particular day or maybe the previous day -- I am not sure -- nine Muslim soldiers had been killed somewhere between Zukici and Bradina. They thought that the Cetniks killed them and told so, and that is why they arrested them and brought them to Celebici. I also whispered into her ear and I asked her which date is it today and she said: "Today it is a holiday, Saint Peter's day." As I know on what date is Saint Peter's day, I knew it was 12th July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did all this happen before the second rape you suffered or after the second rape you have suffered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the second rape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the second rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did these women remain with you in the reception building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those women remained there just for one night, which they spent with us there. The following morning when day broke Mucic came at the door and he said that those women from Zukici that they could go home. So they left and only Grozda and myself remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about the conditions of life inside this reception building for you? Did you receive food regularly during your stay in this reception building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even before, upon our arrival, until then we used to get very little food. After that, as those women from Zukici, after they were taken back home, we did not get any food at all for three days. For three days we did not eat anything. So that I was completely weakened, and I was unable to stand up on my feet. Grozda had to take me to the toilet. When I saw I was so very weak, I asked one of the guards to call the Commander of the camp to come to me so that I could ask him either to let us go home or to kill us, or else to give us something to eat. I do not know whether the guard transmitted that. However, the camp commander did not come, so for three days we were without any food. After that we got one slice of bread, thin as paper. After we got the slice of bread Delic came and he asked why did he seek him and I repeated: "Either let us go or kill us or give us something to eat." He said: "What do you want? You see how it is difficult to fast during Ramadan".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did all this happen before or after the third rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the third rape take place? How much time after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I can't tell you exactly. I do not remember. Maybe not long has passed, but I do not know how many days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Madam, could you please describe in detail the third rape you suffered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One day, it was daylight, he came at the door of our room where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "he came", who came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic came to the door of our room, the room where we were, and as soon as he came through the door he ordered Grozda to go out into the corridor, which was in front of our room. Grozda went out. As he was also armed on that occasion, he also had hand grenades and a pistol and a rifle, but he also had hand grenades on his belt. He started threatening me and I repeated as usual not to touch me, that I was a sick woman. He did not answer anything to that. He only ordered me to take my clothes off. Under pressure and under threat I had to do that. After that he ordered me to go into the bed and lie down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then? Please give us some details about what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he took his clothes off, his trousers. He did not take his boots off, but the trousers were put down to his boots. He went on to the bed and he raped me for the third time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again did he penetrate your vagina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He did penetrate it but he was in a hurry. I could see he did it in a hurry. So he did not stay in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ejaculate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that time as well also on the lower part of my abdomen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he completely undressed during the rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Only his trousers were pulled down. He still kept his shirt and he kept his boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you completely undressed during the rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had only to take my tracksuit off and my underwear, the lower part. I did not have to take the clothes on the upper part of my body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened right after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not allowed to go to the toilet. We had a plastic bowl, which we used to relieve ourselves during the night. We had to urinate into that bowl during the day, and during the day we would -- we were brought water in that bowl and we had to drink out of that bowl.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any further occasion to see Delic after the third rape? Did he come to your room again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes he would just come to the door, threaten us, saying that we would never be released, that we would be killed, and then he would turn around and go. Sometimes he would just come in, open the door, not say anything and straightaway turn his back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any occasion to talk to Delic after the third rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion I only asked him. My sister came. I saw my sister that was taking food to me. I saw her through the window. She was waiting to give food for me, so I asked one of the guards to ask the Commander whether my sister could come inside so that I could ask her about our mother, whether she was alive and how she was. Then Delic went somewhere by car and he pulled up just in front of the window of the corridor and through the window I asked him. I told him: "Commander, sir, please could I meet my sister to enquire about my mother?" Then he told my sister that she could come in, and my sister came and we met so that I could enquire after my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did you suffer any other rape after the three ones you described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. One night, it was very late, there was a guard there was on night duty. Grozdana went to the toilet and that guard who was on duty that evening entered the room where I was. I got scared. I was afraid that another rape would occur or something like that, and I started crying. I said that: "I will call for help." As all the guards were afraid of Delic because he was their commander and they were all scared of him, he became afraid and he went out. He did not abuse me or rape me. He went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not -- do you know the name of this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not know his name. Afterwards I was told that that guard was somewhere from the region of Fojnica. There is a town called Fojnica and that guard was from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, going back for a moment to your third rape, can you say approximately when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I only know that it was after that period when we had no food. When those women from Zukici spent the night, it was also after that, but I do not recall how much time had passed in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs Antic, do you know whether Grozdana Cecez had contraceptive pills with her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Grozdana had that and she was taking that and she also said that she was taking that even before the war and for many years, that she has needed that for many years and she used to take that even before coming to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she ever offer such pills to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When that happened to me, I mean after that second rape, she told me: "Yes, I have that. I used to take that even while she was at home." She told me: "If you'd like me, I will give that to you." I told her I did not need anything like that but I did not say why, because I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell now the court why you did not need such pills, if you do not mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I refused, saying that I did not need that, I did not tell Grozdana the reason why, but I didn't need that because in 1984 I was operated on. I had a tumour, womb tumour. So I did not need that kind of pills, but I did not tell that to Grozda. I was hiding it slightly. Not everybody knew that I had been operated on and that I suffered from that illness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mrs Antic. Can you tell us: did you see any mistreatment of other prisoners during your stay in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One day I saw, while I was going to the toilet, I saw an inmate whose name was Slavko Susic. He was against a big wall, the one wall that could be seen through the window in the corridor where we were. So when I went to the toilet, I saw Slavko leaning against the wall. Next to him was a soldier wearing a camouflage uniform. I recognised Delic. Delic was holding a piece of wood while I was passing by coming back from the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say this to Grozdana?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that to Grozdana and I said: "There is Slavko leaning against the wall." Then Grozdana went out. I don't know. I did not come back. I did not even dare look at what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eyewitness Slavko Susic there against the wall from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him from the window and the door that was the entrance door. As I was going towards the toilet, that's the door leading on to the courtyard. It was made of glass, so I was able to see both through the window and through the door leading out of the building. They opened up on to that wall where Slavko was leaning against.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which distance could you eyewitness this scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It wasn't too far away. I don't know exactly, but not too far away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that going to the toilet and coming back or only going or coming back from the toilet I think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went to the toilet, I saw and when I was going back he was standing in the same spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you recognise Susic? What was his position? Was he facing to the window where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slavko was facing the wall, but since I knew him well, we were very good friends. His wife worked with me before the war, and we visit the each other very often, so I saw when he was led out of the compound, the camp compound to go looking for some radio transmitter. I saw him being taken to the car. He wore a tracksuit and a pair of large boots. They were rolled down, the boots. Since I knew him well from before, I could see that it was Slavko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had a chance to see this scene, did you see whether there were other people with Mr Delic and Mr Susic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was another soldier but I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of what happened to Susic after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe a day or two after that -- I can't remember now -- two days later a guard told us that Slavko had died, that he had died in Number 9. He was in the tunnel that was called Number 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Grozdana go and see this same scene through the window before you or after you or both?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: She has already said that she went and informed Grozdana who was happening so naturally Grozdana saw the incident after she had seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I did not get the answer quite clearly. Okay. Did you have occasion to clean the place around the reception building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Grozdana was taken out more often than I was to sweep in front of the door, so she was going out more often and she was in a better position to see what was happening than I did, but we were never allowed to talk about what we had seen and about what was happening, since there was always somebody in front of the door and we did not dare lest somebody should hear us talking about those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did you know Delic from before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe Delic, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was quite tall. He had short hair. He was balding. He had receding hair. That's more or less it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shown a series of photos a few days ago and were you asked if you could recognise anybody in those photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign a piece of paper containing your answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I have this short statement with photo-spread attachment be marked for identification as Number 90 and shown to the witness for identification purposes, if you do not mind. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can show it to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Could you please put it on the ELMO. Madam, would you please look at the piece of paper on your right, because you have the clear paper on your right. Would the usher show the witness where to look at. Do you recognise your signature on this paper down at the bottom of this paper? You see there are a number of signatures. Is your signature appearing on this paper?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: She should speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. My signature is on that paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Does this paper reflect what you said? I will read it for your convenience: "The witness responded, indicated for the 4 and: "This person seems to be familiar. I am not sure but you must remember it has been five years since it happened, so details are a bit vague, but the features I remember are the forehead, the nose and the mouth. As far as I can remember, since it was some time ago, he looked like the perpetrator of the crime". Does this reflect what you said, Mrs Antic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, your Honour, I would like to tender this statement and the attached photo-spread as Exhibit Number 90 for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Tom Moran for Hazim Delic. We object to the admission of the xeroxed photo-spread, because you can't see anything. It is hard to tell. If they want to admit the original photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Of course we can provide the original photographs if this is your objection, Mr Moran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I would not object to that but the xerox copies are so unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We have no difficulty in attaching the original photo-spread certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to the statement itself, we would object that it is cumulative of what she can testify to. Let her testify to what she saw. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: What is the objection? Is it that it is not her statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No, it is not an objection it is not her statement, not at all. She adopted the statement. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. I do not see what the objection about the statement should be. For the photographs, yes, I think it is possible there may be some doubts. If they can bring the original photographs, it might make things clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as long as the prosecution agrees to substitute the original photographs for the xerox, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We will certainly provide the new attachment. So the exhibit 90 is the statement of the witness and the attachment will be changed as soon as possible and substituted with the original photographs. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It is neater.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr Antic, were you ever formally interrogated by military investigators during your stay in Celebici besides the interrogation of the first day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that happen approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how many days I had already been there. We were called to the building where their command was to be interrogated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in the same room of the rapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was in the same building but not in the same room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say which part of the camp could you see through the window of this room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From that room through the window in that room we could see the building that was called 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you accused of anything specific?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that occasion I was asked about the radio transmitter that they had been looking for when they came to my house. Since they did not find this thing in my house they told me that I kept it in my hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people did interrogate you on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one who interrogated me was my first neighbour, my next-door-neighbour. His name was Mirso Subasic. There was another man with him but I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign any piece of paper after that interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have, but if I signed it, it was under duress. I had to do whatever they wanted me to. Since I was accused of all kinds of things, even of carrying a radio transmitter in my hair, and my hair was always this length, so I felt sorry for my neighbours for accusing me of all those things. I believe that if I had signed something I did that under duress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a long interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly for how long, but it wasn't a very long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any judicial proceedings against you after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Antic, did the Red Cross ever visit the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that several times or one time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They visited for three days, the Red Cross visited the camp, the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but it was in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe these visits? Did they visit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One day, the first day when we saw them enter the compound through the gate, the camp compound, there were two International Red Cross cars and we saw them visit the prisoners who were in tunnel called Number 9 and on that day they visited them and we saw them leave through the gate on their way out, on their way back. Then the next day when they came to the camp again, we saw the same cars enter the camp. We did not see them because they were not parked in that area which we could see from our windows. I was called out to sweep the area outside the door in the courtyard, so I got out and I cleaned and swept the area and I saw the two cars of the International Red Cross.
