They were parked in front of the command building. So I cleaned and one guard was guarding me and I saw that the International Red Cross was supposed to leave at that time. Next to the car there stood Delic. When the International Red Cross, when the people got into their cars, Delic ordered the guard who was guarding me to drive me inside the room where Grozda was. I had to get in. I was afraid. I told Grozda when I got in the room. I said: "We're in trouble, Grozda. They probably are trying to hide our existence. They will probably kill us since they are not allowing them to see us women. It must be because they will kill us". Grozda was also scared. We both started crying. We were afraid that we would be hidden somewhere and killed. The cars left the compound and they left. Then the third day we again saw them enter the compound -- I mean the International Red Cross. Then they visited the prisoners in the Number 6, where those prisoners were located. When they visited those prisoners in Number 6 they asked if there were any women here in the camp and the other prisoners told them about us, so we were visited by them. They came to our room on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked us how we were, how we felt, whether we were abused by anyone, whether anyone touched us, whether we had enough food and hygiene facilities. They asked us everything, about everything, but I could not give them any answers. Grozda was speaking in my name too. Grozda said about me, that I had been raped three times. They asked me if it was true and then I said: "Yes, it was." Then they asked me if this man who was doing that, if he was still there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said that he was still there in the compound and he was some kind of a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Antic, when did you leave Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 31st August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that happen? I mean, were you given a release document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A guard came in the morning. He came at the door and he said that we would be going home that day. We were happy because of that, so that we were waiting to be called and to be told to get ready, and after a short while another guard came to the door and he said that we should follow him. So we went with the guard who brought us to the building where the command was. He took us into a room and Pavo Mucic was sitting there, and he released us and he told us that we would be going home. He issued us with some kind of a release document indicating that we were allowed to go home, that he was setting us free and that we were free to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was exactly the person who gave you the release form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom was the release form signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he sign that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you gave this document to the prosecution a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would mark for identification this release form as Exhibit Number 91 and 91A and then submit it to the witness for identification purposes, if you allow me. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Could you place on the ELMO the original, please? Ms Antic, would you please watch the document which is on your right. Is this your release form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did fill this document as for the limitation of your movements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was filled in by Mucic. Mucic wrote down that my freedom of movement was limited to Konjic and Pokojiste. Pokojiste is where my mother had fled from her home and I asked if possible at all if it is possible, if he could also put down my village, Idbar, to limit my freedom of movement to Konjic, Pokojiste and Idbar, so that I could go to my garden and bring some produce back, since my sister -- my mother was with my sister -- since my sister had taken in a lot of refugees. I wasn't sure whether we would have enough food for all of us. So I asked him is it at all possible for him to limit my movements to Idbar and he did that to me, so that he wrote down Konjic, Pokojiste, Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which role did Mr Mucic have inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the camp he was in charge. He was asked about everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the camp, did Mr Mucic ever ask you about your treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other times besides the one you already told us, any other time in which you know Mr Mucic was at the camp, inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He arrived on one other occasion to our room. Mucic came to our room on one other occasion. He brought in a girl. She was Grozda's -- she was from Grozda's brother-in-law, so he brought her in to visit Grozda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. This concludes my examination-in-chief of witness Antic. I am sorry. I tender as exhibit 91 and 91A for admission? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Has the defence seen the release documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I have seen it and I have absolutely no objection to it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I would like to see it myself and I would like to show it to my client, if I may, please. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: We have no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I think you have received it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I have not received it. I have received a translation of it but not a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am sorry. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The original, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would your Honours forgive me for a moment if I turn my back on you, please? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes, I have no objection to that document. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The document is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am concluded. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I do not think we could start any cross-examination now, the end of the day. I think we can continue with cross-examination when we come on the 14th. (5.30 pm)
